title: Vintage Gibson SG Custom Value Guide: Prices By Year
description: SG Custom values from $3,000 to $22,000 across early white and later walnut guitars. Compare years, three-pickup originality, hardware and repairs.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Custom Value Guide
alt: Walnut-finish Gibson SG Custom with three covered pickups, gold hardware and a Bigsby vibrato

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Custom Worth?
faqs.a: Vintage Gibson SG Custom reference values run from $2,450 to $4,050 for typical 1970s walnut guitars to $12,600 to $27,400 for early white small-guard examples, reviewed in October 2026. Three original humbuckers, factory finish and an unbroken neck remain the starting point.

faqs.q: Does The Large-Guard Range Mean White And Walnut Are Equally Valuable?
faqs.a: No. The $2,850 to $12,600 range covers played white and walnut guitars. An original white finish can add collector interest, but condition, repairs and retained parts also affect the appraisal. The combination of finish and condition determines its position within the range.

faqs.q: Is A Bigsby Wrong On A 1970s SG Custom?
faqs.a: No. Factory Bigsby versions exist alongside stopbar configurations. The original mounting, parts and finish history determine whether the hardware belongs to the guitar.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Change Gibson SG Custom Value?
faqs.a: Yes. The ranges assume the original finish described in the condition notes. A full refinish changes the collector category, so I assess the finish work, retained parts and repairs individually. The reduction depends on the quality of the work, era and retained original parts.

faqs.q: How Can I Get My Gibson SG Custom Appraised?
faqs.a: Send clear front and back photographs, both sides of the headstock, the pickups, bridge, case and any known repairs. Keep removed original parts with the instrument and include the history you know. Those details support an individual appraisal.
